classification.difficultyReason: Translate all marked perpendicular pairs into notation without inferring extra properties from appearance.

inlines.text: Name all the pairs of perpendicular lines in the following diagrams.

spec.description: Three complete segments AB, CD and EF cross at an unlabelled centre. AB is steeply descending rightward; CD rises rightward; EF descends rightward more shallowly. A square is between the rays towards C and F. No dots or terminal arrows.
spec.mathematics: CD perpendicular EF; AB has no perpendicularity mark.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied blue statement is answer evidence only.

answer.worked: $CD\perp EF$: the square between the rays towards $C$ and $F$ marks a right angle.

spec.description: LK vertical and LM horizontal share L; LN rises rightward inside their right angle and passes through the square region. No bisector marks, dots or arrows.
spec.mathematics: KL perpendicular LM. LN is not an angle bisector given.

answer.worked: $KL\perp LM$: the square at $L$ marks the angle between $LK$ and $LM$ as a right angle.

spec.description: AB rises rightward from B; BC descends steeply rightward; CD rises rightward from C and extends slightly beyond C to the lower left. Squares at B and C. No dots, arrows or parallel markers.
spec.mathematics: AB perpendicular BC and BC perpendicular CD.

answer.worked: $AB\perp BC$ from the square at $B$. $BC\perp CD$ from the square at $C$.

spec.description: Triangle PQR with P upper left, Q upper right and R lower left. PQ horizontal, PR vertical, RQ diagonal. Unfilled interior right-angle square at P.
spec.mathematics: RP perpendicular PQ. No numerical lengths or angles beyond the right-angle mark are supplied.

answer.worked: $RP\perp PQ$: the square at $P$ marks a right angle.

spec.description: Four lines share an unlabelled centre: vertical PT, horizontal VR, descending WS and rising UQ. An upper-right square between P and R is crossed by the ray to Q; a rotated lower-left square between W and U is crossed by the ray to V. Eight italic endpoint labels, no dots or arrows.
spec.mathematics: PT perpendicular VR and WS perpendicular UQ. P is an endpoint, not the centre, so the source answer PT perpendicular PR is unsupported.
spec.answerVisibility: Question geometry only; authored answer is flagged for editorial review.

answer.worked: $PT\perp VR$ from the square between the vertical and horizontal lines. $WS\perp UQ$ from the rotated square between the rays towards $W$ and $U$.

spec.description: Two oblique lines rise rightward and extend beyond A,B and D,C respectively. AD and BC descend rightward between them. Interior squares at A and C only. No parallel markers, dots or arrows.
spec.mathematics: AB perpendicular AD and BC perpendicular DC are marked. Apparent parallelism supplies no additional given; no squares are added at B or D.

answer.worked: $AB\perp AD$ from the square at $A$. $BC\perp DC$ from the square at $C$.
